description: Rights-based governance coordinates food water soil biodiversity and livelihoods.
Watershed restoration links local knowledge basin institutions and ecological repair.
Water rights aquifer governance drought allocation and basin coordination become central.
Digital tools are governed for access data rights accountability and ecological monitoring.
Public reserves safety nets nutrition support and early warning reduce crisis exposure.
Production policy outpaces soil water biodiversity and livelihood safeguards.
Weak tenure and land financialization undermine rights stewardship and legitimacy.
Weak institutions allow extraction pollution land degradation and public harm.
